# Formalization coverage and dependency ledger

The objective is to formalize **all mathematical results in the repository's
surreal, surcomplex and omnific-integer documents**, including their hypotheses and size
restrictions. This ledger starts from the main reports; it is not a reduction
of that objective to the statements easiest to count or prove.

The implementation plan is the foundations report,
[`foundations/article.tex`](foundations-and-computation/foundations/article.tex),
especially `found:sec:architecture`, `found:sub:layers`,
`found:sub:contracts`, and `found:sub:milestones`. The report describes a
proposal, not an existing implementation. The preserved Lean sketches under
its `code/` directory are source artifacts; their presence does not establish
that the current Lean target compiles or imports them.

## Scope and how to read this ledger

examples, equations, prose assertions and companion proofs contain further
claims. Counts are a navigation aid, **not a completeness certificate**.
The foundations report has 31 numbered result/example/principle environments,
including seven examples and one design principle; the narrower inventory
counts its 23 standard results.

Statuses are deliberately strict:

- **Pending**: no checked Lean theorem has yet been mapped to the entire source
  statement, with all its hypotheses and conclusions.
- **Prerequisites proved**: some reusable algebra or an abstract conditional
  theorem is checked; the full source statement remains pending.
- **Proved**: an imported, compiled Lean declaration matches the full statement,
  and its axiom dependencies have been inspected. A conditional theorem counts
  only for its stated hypotheses; instantiation at surreal numbers needs its
  own checked construction or bridge.
- **Needs correction**: a stated claim is false or underspecified as written;
  record the counterexample or missing hypothesis before formalizing a corrected
  statement. Never conceal this state with `axiom`, `sorry`, or an impossible
  typeclass assumption.

The main-report index is **pending unless mapped below**, with the
implementation table recording progress at the precise clause level.
A checked abstract theorem is not a construction of the surreal ordered field
or a normal-form bridge.

No mathematical statement or arithmetic definition is changed. Its field
construction is included in the transitive axiom audit. An explicit order

and its already constructed additive structure. Transporting multiplication
and inverse gives a proved ordered field on that same sign carrier.
Finite normal forms now embed faithfully in the actual sign field, preserving
valuation, leading coefficient and positivity. Canonical cut evaluation of
arbitrary small formal forms now gives an ordered field isomorphism with
inverse extraction, exact real monomials, and finite-evaluation agreement.
Small divisible workspaces now contain every small formal family, and their
odd-degree roots prove real closedness of the formal and actual sign fields.
Small strong real and complex sums, their algebraic operations, actual
valuation/leading data/standard part, and exponent-workspace coherence are
proved below. Actual univariate formal evaluation and its composition law
are also constructed, including finite-variable evaluation. Recentered ordinary
real and complex analytic Taylor lifting preserves sums, products and correctly
recentered composition; the Taylor strong-sum rule determines it uniquely on
its finite analytic domain. Fine derivatives are proved for polynomials,
formal evaluation at every infinitesimal point, and recentered Taylor lifts throughout their ordinary monads. The generic
chain, reciprocal and quotient rules are proved. Finite sine and cosine agree
with their separate strong Taylor sums and ordinary analytic lifts; their
fine derivatives, including the real-parameter derivative of phase, are proved.
Lifted analytic germs have the exact leading-monomial relative error, valuation and leading coefficient, and their
real signs are decided by that monomial. Ordinary analytic nonnegativity now
lifts to every actual surreal point in a closed ordinary interval, including
its endpoints. The complete univariate local-calculus and sign-lifting
proposition is proved below. Multivariable analytic lifting and universe
coherence remain separate obligations.

The limit is built by the source's exact coefficient stabilization, isolated as a sequential statement for any linearly ordered `Γ` and any `V` with zero: if, for each cutoff `R`, all sufficiently late terms agree at every exponent `≤ R`, then some Hahn series agrees eventually with the sequence at every exponent `≤ R`, for each `R`, and that series is unique. ## Dependency order

1. **Size guards and finite algebra (Layer A).** First prove the unrestricted
   bound/cut contradictions (`found:prop:allcuts`) for an irreflexive relation.
   Define complexification of a commutative ring with multiplication
   `(a,b)(c,d) = (ac-bd, ad+bc)`, its scalar embedding, `i`, conjugation and norm
   square. Prove coordinate identities, involution, norm multiplicativity and
   Gram's identity before introducing order. Ordered-field positivity then
   justifies inverses; real closedness is an additional prerequisite for square
   roots and algebraic closedness. Source anchors: `found:eq:pairmul`,
   `found:eq:conj`, `found:eq:pairinv`, `found:prop:complex`, `found:eq:gram`,
   `found:eq:rationalcircle`, `trigonometry:eq:dotcross`, and
   `trigonometry:eq:gram`. The full `found:prop:complex` also asserts real-closed
   and class-coded conclusions; coordinate algebra alone does not complete it.
2. **Ordered algebra and finite polynomial consequences.** Establish the rational
   unit-circle parametrization and reusable finite linear/polynomial algebra.
   Factorization needs algebraic closedness; norm geometry needs the appropriate
   ordered/real-closed input. Early polynomial targets include
   `polynomial:thm:fta` and `polynomial:thm:crt`, followed by the finite-algebra
   descent theorem `found:thm:finitepoints`. Keep generic proofs separate from
   their surreal specializations.
3. **Set-sized Hahn support and evaluation (Layer B).** Prove well-ordering and
   local finiteness for admissible support families, support-preserving sums,
   positive-support geometric/binomial series, and admissible substitution.
   Then define standard part and Taylor lifting with recentering. Initial
   anchors include `polynomial:lem:support`, `trigonometry:lem:support`,
   `found:prop:positive`, and `found:cor:fixeddomain`.
4. **Coefficient rings and coherent functions (Layer C).** Give separate types
   to the four coefficient-ring conventions in the document map. Establish
   coefficientwise differentiation/integration and support-controlled
   composition, then local division/preparation, finite deformations, and
   residue duality. The analytic-geometry ring table must be checked before
   transporting any theorem between these types. Follow with contours and
   Stokes, global divisors, and the remaining polynomial/trigonometric results.
5. **Universe-indexed surreal construction and bridge (Layer D, independent
   foundational track).** Construct or import a checked numeric-game/sign
   development, with birthdays and a visible size bound. Prove field and order
   laws, real closedness, normal forms, monomials, and compatibility of admissible
   sums. Then prove `found:thm:workspace`. The eight surreal reports branch here:
   graph results need game representations; birthday and broadcast results
   need sign/ordinal arithmetic; evaluation and genetic-gap results need their
   specified supports or differentiation semantics. The plan's two tracks allow
   local Hahn mathematics to proceed before this bridge is finished.
   The [infinite normal-form bridge note](NORMAL_FORM_BRIDGE.md) records the
   verified upstream APIs, the canonical order isomorphism and inverse
   extraction and arithmetic, actual closedness, small real strong sums and exponent
   coherence, and the remaining Taylor and universe-coherence obligations.
   Approximation alone does not give uniqueness or arithmetic compatibility.
6. **Topology and further structure (Layer E).** Define the intended fine
   topology over the actual carrier and prove small-index discreteness alongside
   the larger-index counterexample. Prove finite-angle lifting, distinguish
   derivative notions, and supply any real exponential/global character as
   separate proved structures. Only after a universe-coherent/class
   interpretation is established can full-class all-scale rigidity and its
   consequences be claimed.

This is a dependency order, not a promise to process reports in file order.
A substantial theorem should be split into its simplest necessary lemmas while
retaining an explicit obligation for every conclusion of the source theorem.

Both inputs to Mathlib's `IsRealClosed.of_linearOrderedField` are now proved
for actual sign surreals: genetic nonnegative square roots and odd-degree
roots transported from a small divisible Hahn coefficient workspace.
Actual sign-field standard part, Conway monomials and weighted finite
coefficient scaling are now constructed. General finite-family coprime
factor linearization is a proved equivalence, using Mathlib’s Sylvester map
for the binary inverse. Translation to monic depressed form, the
actual polynomial scaling and reduction, and the ordinary-real coprime
factorization with a proper odd-degree factor are now constructed. The
binary lift in arbitrarily many formal parameters is now constructed as an actual
polynomial factorization over power series, with uniqueness, coprimeness and
exact degrees. Evaluation at finitely many positive-order Hahn inputs is a
proved algebra homomorphism with an explicit support certificate.
These constructions now give full finite-family, support-controlled coprime
factor lifting in arbitrary ordered Hahn fields, including the documented
common support monoid and unrestricted uniqueness. The ordered field
normal-form bridge and small-workspace localization transfer the resulting
Hahn odd-degree roots to actual surreals. Localizing both coordinates also
transfers complex Hahn roots to actual surcomplex numbers. Small real and complex strong
sums are now defined through their canonical coefficients and agree with
workspace evaluation. Univariate and finite-variable formal substitution are proved.
Recentered complex analytic germs and their sum/product laws are constructed;
fine differentiation is proved at zero and ordinary centers, with general
re-expansion, composition and multivariable analytic lifting still pending.
Conway's normalization and factor-lifting route is in
[*On Numbers and Games*, Theorems 23–28, pp. 40–42](https://kyl.neocities.org/books/%5BTEC%20CON%5D%20on%20numbers%20and%20games.pdf);
the universal ordered-field embedding there uses real closedness and cannot
be used circularly to obtain these roots. The finite-parameter strong-evaluation
bridge is now proved for ordinary coefficients; the remaining analytic
operation and nonordinary-center derivative correspondences are separate. Small-index convergence in the native fine topology
cannot replace strong Hahn summability.

## Soundness boundaries that must survive translation

- **Permitted cuts:** a type in one universe cannot fill cuts indexed by its
  whole own carrier. Smaller-index cut data must remain explicit. The abstract
  obstruction does not by itself construct legitimate surreal cuts or prove
  `found:lem:bounds` for surreal numbers.
- **Complex multiplication:** the default product ring on `F × F` has the
  wrong multiplication and identity. Use the actual quadratic extension or a
  dedicated structure; see `found:rem:productring`.
- **Class versus workspace:** proving a theorem for a fixed Hahn field is useful
  but does not supply a universal field of all surreal numbers. Workspace
  localization and preservation of the operations used need separate proofs.
- **Two near-mirror series:** `found:ex:rescaling` uses coefficients `t^(-n²)`
  and fails evaluation at every nonzero argument in the fixed rational value
  group; `found:ex:internal` uses `t^(n²)` and is nonpolynomial despite internal
  all-scale coherence. Full-class rigidity cannot be specialized to a fixed
  value group without its missing dominating-scale hypothesis.
- **Strong sums:** well-ordered support and finite coefficient contributions
  are both required. Formal identities are not topological limits. Taylor
  lifting at `r + ε` uses the Taylor series centered at `r`, not unrestricted
  Maclaurin substitution (`found:rem:recentering`).
- **Different analytic categories:** radius-free coefficient germs, a fixed
  ordinary domain, common-domain germs, and formal coefficient series are
  distinct rings. The analysis merge records inequivalent function classes and
  inequivalent residues; a common name does not authorize a common definition.
- **Different geometries:** Hahn valuation and ordered modulus have distinct
  root and contour statements. A contour representing a residue series is an
  extra theorem, not the definition of the series functional.
- **Topology and size:** small-set discreteness (`found:thm:discrete`) coexists
  with a larger-index nonconstant convergent net (`found:ex:largerindex`). Do not
  assert eventual constancy for arbitrary index types or silently introduce an
  ordinary metric for the fine topology (`found:lem:nometric`).
- **Overlapping birthday results:** the two Gonshor reports prove the same
  inequality on different domains, neither containing the other. The shared
  `R[[ω⁻¹]]` case can reuse a proof once equivalence is established, but both
  domain statements remain obligations.
- **Independent proof notions:** fine derivative, formal power-series germ,
  Hahn-coherent datum and scalar-field derivation must retain separate types
  and explicit comparison theorems.

`T`, `L`, `P`, `C` mean literal `theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition` and
`corollary` environments; examples, computations, assessments and other
custom environments are not included. A label inside a nested equation
labels that equation, not the enclosing theorem or proposition; an
environment without its own label is indexed by its source line.

### Corrections found while formalizing the placed reports

Each item below was reported by a formalization survey and then confirmed
independently by two reviewers, each of whom read the statement, its
standing conventions and its proof and tried to refute the claim. The source
corrections below have now been made and checked against the local proofs.
This records corrected prose and hypotheses, not new Lean coverage.

- **Corrected in source** (`prony:sec:sharp` and the literature comparison in the
  [Prony report](surcomplex/prony-reconstruction-at-surreal-scales/article.tex)):
  the unit-weight single-cluster formulas now require `n ≥ 2`.
  For `n = 1` the empty-sum and empty-maximum conventions give
  `d₁ = δ₁ = 0` and `Θ = v(w₁)`, hence `Θ = 0` for a valuation-zero weight.
- **Corrected in source** (`tate:thm:coordinates` and the corresponding clauses
  in `tate:thm:main` and `tate:node:thm:main`, in
  [Hahn–Tate uniformization](surcomplex/hahn-tate-uniformization/article.tex)):
  the coordinate-family domain clause now requires `u ∈ K^×` (or `𝕂^×`
  in the general coefficient field). At `u = 0` both bilateral coordinate
  families are identically zero and strongly summable although `0 ∉ U_q`.
  The report now explains this exception; the README and catalogue agree.
- **Corrected in source** (discussion of `tate:eq:circlelayers` in
  [Hahn–Tate uniformization](surcomplex/hahn-tate-uniformization/article.tex)):
  the rank-one circle quotient is `(H_α/H_α^-)/ℤᾱ`. The full quotient
  `H_α/ℤα` retains kernel `H_α^-`, even when the rank-one value group is
  `ℝ`. The example `Γ = ℝ ⊕lex ℝ`, `α = (1,0)` makes that kernel explicit.
  The introductory description now also distinguishes the kernels of
  `v mod H_α^-` on `K_{H_α}` and `v mod H_α` on `K_Γ`.
- **Corrected in source** (`tate:theta:eq:zerorow` in
  [Hahn–Tate uniformization](surcomplex/hahn-tate-uniformization/article.tex)):
  the zero-row equation now uses `ξ₀`, the coarse reduction of the full
  solution `ξ`. Substituting `ξ₀` into the full coupled theta sum leaves
  leading term `−2 τ₁² τ₂⁻³` from lattice index `(−1,1)`, so the higher
  rows cannot be discarded. The displayed finite expansion of `ξ` remains
  valid, since the difference has positive first-coordinate valuation.
- **Clarified in source** (`diff:aut:lem:evaluation` and
  `diff:aut:lem:projective`, in
  [differential equations](surcomplex/differential-equations/article.tex)):
  formal maps used as inverse maps on infinitesimal tuples explicitly
  have zero constant term. The projective properness comparison is
  applied over the set-sized field generated by finitely many coordinates,
  with its induced valuation ring, rather than over a proper-class field.
  The direct reduction and local uniqueness proofs remain elementary;
  no new Lean coverage is claimed.
- **Clarified in source** (`diff:rs:sub:procedure`, in
  [differential equations](surcomplex/differential-equations/article.tex)):
  the finite regular-singular procedure requires effective coefficient
  operations as well as finite rational support. Complex algebraic
  entries give a concrete sufficient input class; arbitrary named complex
  constants do not by themselves provide exact spectral, equality and
  order operations. The finite-dependence theorem retains its full
  mathematical scope. The reduced weight set is now proved closed under
  all predecessor pairs, and the no-resonance case retains residual
  nilpotent blocks. No new Lean coverage is claimed.
- **Clarified in source** (`diff:rs:conv:alphabet`, in
  [differential equations](surcomplex/differential-equations/article.tex)):
  a gauge field is explicitly Euler-stable and contains `ℂ`. Translation
  by `∂ = −t∂_τ` always gives an identity in `No[i]`, but a system over
  a smaller Euler-stable field need not translate to a system over that
  field. For `E = K_(ℤ√2)`, the Euler equation `∂_τ y = y` has
  coefficient in `E`, whereas its intrinsic coefficient `−t` is outside
  `E`. The source now distinguishes this from the same-field equivalence
  when `t ∈ E`. No additional Lean coverage is claimed.
- **Corrected in source** (`diff:rs:lem:euler`, in
  [differential equations](surcomplex/differential-equations/article.tex)):
  `∂ = -t∂_T` preserves `K_Γ` exactly when `Γ = {0}` or `1 ∈ Γ`.
  The proof handles the constant field separately and derives `1 ∈ Γ`
  from the derivative of a nonconstant monomial in every nonzero group.
  The Euler derivative can delete the constant term, so its support is
  contained in the original support, rather than always equal to it.
- **Corrected in source** (`markov:prop:reversible`, in
  [Markov generators](surreal/markov-generators-at-every-scale/article.tex)):
  the converse now specifies a strictly coarsening chain from the discrete
  partition to the one-block partition, a strictly positive probability
  vector `π₀`, and strictly increasing scales. The proof gives the weighted
  matrices, verifies their endpoints and strict rank drops, and handles
  the one-state case. Without the final endpoint, the chain
  `{{1},{2},{3}} > {{1,2},{3}}` would end in rank `2`, contrary to an
  irreducible generator's rank-one final plateau.
- **Corrected in source** (`ihs:hh:prop:inner`, `ihs:sec:sharednot` and
  `ihs:rf:rem:nodiv`, in
  [infinite-dimensional spectral theory](surcomplex/infinite-dimensional-hahn-spectral-theory/article.tex)):
  the claim that divisibility is necessary to define the Part I norm has
  been removed. For `δ = v(x)`, the proof factors
  `⟨x,x⟩ = ‖x_δ‖² t^{2δ}(1+u)` and constructs its positive root
  `‖x_δ‖ t^δ (1+u)^{1/2}` by the near-one binomial series.
  This proposition and the scalar modulus work for every ordered value
  group. For `Γ = ℤ` and an ordinary unit vector `e`, `‖te‖ = t`,
  even though the positive scalar `t` has no square root. A subsequent
  review of the Part I proofs removes their unused standing divisibility
  restriction. The closed-range theorem `ihs:hh:thm:closedrange` now holds
  at every rank: its range is the kernel of the continuous defect projection,
  whose nonnegative support gives `v(Πx) ≥ v(x)`. Only the real-valued
  metric-completeness subsection assumes `Γ ⊆ ℝ`. These strengthened
  source statements are not new Lean coverage.
- The closing clause of `ihs:rf:prop:algebra` in
  [infinite-dimensional spectral theory](surcomplex/infinite-dimensional-hahn-spectral-theory/article.tex)
  now requires two distinct indices before asserting that `𝒜_rf` has zero
  divisors. The proof exhibits the nonzero constant matrix units `E_ii` and
  `E_jj`, whose product is zero. Part II still assumes only that `I` is
  nonempty; for a singleton, the source identifies `R_I = ℂ` and
  `𝒜_rf = ℂ((t^Γ)) = K`, a field. The conditional zero-divisor assertion is
  proved in [RowColumnFinite.lean](../Surreal/HahnSeries/RowColumnFinite.lean).
  This source correction resolves the reported exception without narrowing
  the algebra, action, involution or valuation-inequality statements. The
  singleton identification is not separately mapped to a Lean equivalence.

- **Needs correction**, not yet made in the source (last sentence of
  `ent:mv:thm:exceptional`, in
  [entire functions at arbitrary rank](surcomplex/entire-functions-at-arbitrary-rank/article.tex)):
  "For `d = 2` the set `Pdir(F)` is at most countable" stands as a separate
  sentence after the conditional "If `F` is not a polynomial, ...", and the
  theorem opens with "For every `F`". For `F = 0`, or any polynomial, every
  restriction `F(Tc)` is a polynomial, so `Pdir(F) = P¹(ℂ)` is uncountable. The
  proof uses that a proper algebraic subset of `P¹(ℂ)` is finite, which needs
  `F` nonpolynomial, and `ent:mv:cor:countable` already assumes it. The fix is to
  move the clause into the nonpolynomial sentence. Three independent reviewers
  confirmed this; the proof and its uses need no other change.

The subsequent Part II source review also corrects the comparison of its
coherent diagonal algebra with `K^I`: equality holds for finite `I` or
trivial `Γ`, and strict inclusion requires infinite `I` and nonzero `Γ`.
Its projection calculus is vectorwise Hahn-additive; lack of an
operator-valued Hahn sum does not rule out a classical spectral measure.
The revised `ihs:rf:rem:notopsum` gives the relevant counterexample instead:
over `Γ = ℚ`, coordinate partial sums of
`Σₙ t^{1−1/(n+1)} eₙ` fail to converge in valuation. These corrections
add no Lean coverage.

A sixth confirmed report, that `tail:lem:signs` needs `char M ≠ 2` (in
characteristic `2`, `√(a+1) = √a + 1` over `𝔽₂(a)`), was already corrected in the
source by `506cd11`.

Two further reports were refuted by both reviewers and need no correction.
`meas:lem:prony`, where "a monic polynomial with distinct roots, all in `Ω`"
carries the standard meaning that it splits with simple roots in `Ω`; and the
field-generality remark in `hol:sec:fields`, since the generic point of the
several-variable proof can be taken in the uncountable field
`K = k((t^Γ))` itself (`Γ ≠ 0` by `hol:conv:group`).
A second survey raised two more reports, and three reviewers refuted each. The
remark after `prony:cor:nonlinear` inherits the corollary's hypotheses, including
the lattice criterion `prony:eq:latticecriterion`, so its nonlinear clause is
covered by `prony:eq:latticeimage`; the proposed counterexample violates that
criterion. In `tate:prop:tail`, `X_q` and `Y_q` are defined only off `q^ℤ`
(`tate:thm:main`) and the retained isolated terms only for `u ≠ 1`, so the
statement has no content at `u = 1`; its tail bound also holds there termwise.

The critical-potential source review corrects `diff:cp:rem:stagezero`
and its introductory comparison: `Q_{1,0} = ¼ω⁻² = Q_{0,¼}` belongs to
`ℂ((t^ℝ))`. Among stages `α ≥ 1`, the potential leaves that field exactly
when `(α,c) ≠ (1,0)`: the surviving exponent `−2−2ω⁻¹` is outside `ℝ`.
The original blanket exclusion was false. The Liouville identity
`diff:cp:lem:gauge` is now stated over an arbitrary characteristic-zero
differential field with `c` in that field; no constant assumption is needed
until the subsequent Euler classification. These source corrections add
no Lean coverage; the critical-potential results remain **Pending**.

The Sections 39–40 source review clarifies `diff:cp:ex:omegaexpansion`:
the exact Hahn sum determines `Q_ω`; prescribing its coefficients at the
finite logarithmic scales still permits smaller remainders. It also
strengthens `diff:cp:prop:gaps` with an explicit failure of logarithm
closure in `H_{Δ₂}`: `ℓ_λ` lies in the field but `log ℓ_λ = ℓ_{λ+1}` does
not, because its Conway exponent has inner support beyond `λ`.
These are source-level support arguments; their Lean coverage remains
**Pending**.

### September 23 omnific-integer additions

The documents placed in `be06fc8` add [omnific Diophantine geometry](surreal/omnific-diophantine-geometry/article.tex)
and [set-sized quotients of the omnific integers](surreal/set-sized-quotients-of-omnific-integers/article.tex).
At placement these added 75 literal standard results, plus three custom
`maintheorem` statements. The elementary review and first Diophantine assembly
in `bbdd536` increased its count to 67. The subsequent written expansions
(`0240140`, `7494d53`, `3daef3c`, `b829d8b`, `aae58bb`) gave 143
Diophantine and 227 quotient standard results before the batch-28 expansions.
The current counts appear in the inventory. Statements remain **Pending** in Lean except for the implementation mappings below.

The Diophantine proof review covers its original Sections 1–12, now
Sections 1–10, 14 and 19, excluding the newly inserted material in Sections 6 and 10. It includes complex separated-power rigidity, the
corrected divisibility identity, quadratic polarization, coordinate ideals,
bounded-set transfer for quantified formulas, induction-domain restrictions,
primitive real directions and finite ordered specialization. The polynomial-arc
theorem permits real coefficients and real-coefficient auxiliary expressions.
The root review adds a finite-factorization proof of the two-term root
obstruction and clarifies nonmonic divisibility, binomial supports and the
different domains of the two residue maps. These source-level extensions
remain **Pending** in Lean. The new Section 11 has now received a proof
review of its degree algebra, ideal predicate, Pell divisibility,
intersectivity and integer definitions. It distinguishes intermediate
rings from full positive-support rings with explicit boundary examples.
Section 12 has now received a proof review of the detector, ideal test,
constant-term graph and number-field extension. In
`odg:def:rem:numberfieldideal`, the existing root hypothesis already supplies
an integer radicand for a one-witness existential ideal and six-witness
existential graph. This further combined consequence remains **Pending**
in Lean, as do the original claims. New material in Section 10,
Sections 16–18 and 20–21, new curve pointers in Sections 6, 7 and 14,
and remaining source reconciliation still need review.
Section 13 has now received a proof review of fraction interpretation,
coefficient reconstruction, automorphisms and logical consequences. Its
reconstruction extends to the number-field ideal predicates, and the
finite-system c.e.-set classification extends to every characteristic-zero
coefficient field via the order-free integer guard. These combined
consequences are also **Pending** in Lean. Sections 15.1–15.4 now have a
proof review of denominator ideals, least denominators, the multiplier
theorem and the affine dichotomy. Translation at zero is restored and
the denominator-equivalence remark excludes infinity. These arguments
remain **Pending** in Lean. The subsequent Sections 15.5–15.7 review
expands rational-function and curve applications and the focusing/density
proofs. It corrects the zero focusing parameter and projective-point
wording, and specifies the topology at infinity. The fixed field `R(t)`
is discrete in the induced surreal topology, unlike its degree topology,
by the preceding degree and set-cut lemmas. This consequence is also
**Pending** in Lean. The Sections 15.8–15.12 review corrects the false
claim that standard part and rational residue agree only on `ℚ`:
their agreement locus is `ℚ` plus their joint kernel, which contains
nonzero infinitesimals. The scale-defect and Tor proofs now make the
module maps explicit; the defect has infinite module length despite
finite real dimension. Fixed-workspace and Gaussian arguments are
expanded, including nonzero-denominator choice for constant projective
directions. All remain **Pending** in Lean.
The four Diophantine companions and fifteen quotient companions from the earlier
placements are now assembled; the entire-function rectification addition is
also written. These assemblies are distinct from proof review and formalization.

The two reports placed in `f4c9504`,
[omnific-preserving automorphisms](surreal/omnific-preserving-automorphisms/article.tex)
and [omnific groups and lattices](surreal/omnific-groups-and-lattices/article.tex),
are now assembled with prefixed labels. Their proof review and Lean results
remain **Pending**. The three reports placed in `a4dcb91` now incorporate
their companions as recorded above; the index covers their assembled texts
without claiming proof review or Lean coverage.

The Diophantine report supplies a dependency plan in `odg:sec:formal`: define
the support-restricted omnific subring and constant-term retraction, then
finite quotients, product/norm rigidity, quadratic identities and the quartic
integrality guard. Its global common-divisor and denominator-clearing claims
require actual small-cut bounds and must remain separate from results in a
fixed Hahn workspace. The quotient report additionally requires explicit
universe and target-cardinality bounds: a universal statement about set-sized
targets cannot be replaced by one about all targets in the same universe as
a fixed carrier. These obligations extend the existing goal.

The added Gaussian-fiber and étale-norm arguments in Section 6 have now
received a proof review against sources 07 and 13. The proofs make support
admissibility, parameter uniqueness, finite splitting and coefficient
extension explicit. Further proved consequences give proper-class fibers
for nonzero kernels at an ordinary point and extend étale norm rigidity
to abstract Hahn rings in arbitrary characteristic. Explicit zero-level,
nilpotent and purely inseparable examples delimit the hypotheses. These
prose consequences remain **Pending** in Lean; the actual ring package
is mapped as **Proved** above. A subsequent pass reviews source 07's
quartic (`odg:def:rem:quarticvariant`) and the elementary ring/Euler
subsections 16.2–16.3 (`odg:cr:lem:rings`, `odg:cr:lem:euler`,
`odg:cr:lem:separation`, `odg:cr:cor:algclosed`). It supplies the
intermediate-ring proof, the valuation-ring and residue details, and
corrects two supporting prose assertions: for the zero exponent group
the one-sided ring is a field, and the Euler image inclusion need not
be proper. It also proves the logarithmic-derivative residue formula
`ct(∂_λ u/u) = λ(deg u)` for nonzero Hahn series. These results remain
**Pending** in Lean. The next pass reviews Section 16.4, including
`odg:cr:lem:division`, `odg:cr:thm:squarefree`, `odg:cr:prop:cubic`,
`odg:cr:cor:weierstrass`, `odg:cr:cor:generalweierstrass` and
`odg:cr:prop:singular`. Differential division now states `m ≥ 1`;
the cubic proposition distinguishes its universal polynomial identity
from the formula requiring a nonzero discriminant. Its proof and the
following prose correct the differential normalization, explain regularity
at `y = 0` and supply the missing zero-parameter case for singular cubics.
These results remain **Pending** in Lean. The subsequent pass reviews
the rest of Section 16, including `odg:cr:lem:separated`,
`odg:cr:thm:annihilation`, `odg:cr:lem:constantpoint`, `odg:cr:thm:proper`,
`odg:cr:cor:hahnproper`, `odg:cr:thm:symmetric`, `odg:cr:cor:semiample`
and `odg:cr:prop:inherit`. It specifies positive symmetric degree and
expands pullback compatibility, constant descent and tangent evaluation.
Prose consequences extend proper rigidity to globally generated Kähler
differentials without smoothness and symmetric rigidity to arbitrary
separating data; a finite-cover argument identifies tangent detection
with tautological semiampleness for smooth projective schemes.
All these claims remain **Pending** in Lean. Imported scheme foundations
are cited and their hypotheses checked; full foundational proof review,
the curve classification in Section 17 and subsequent applications remain
outside that pass. A further pass reviews Sections 17.1–17.2, from
`odg:cr:lem:canonical` through `odg:cr:cor:allcurves`. It makes the closed-point
and finite-puncture hypotheses explicit, corrects the circle's two conjugate
boundary points, and supplies descent across arbitrary field extensions.
The logarithmic proof identifies a closed boundary centre and compares the same
contraction in both support rings. These results remain **Pending** in Lean;
arithmetic fibers in Section 17.3 and subsequent applications were outside that
pass. The next pass reviews Section 17.3, from `odg:cr:thm:arith` through
`odg:cr:thm:descent`, including closed affine presentations, nonflat models,
denominator clearing and injectivity of integer polynomial arcs. It separates
set-sized workspace fibers from proper-class fibers and proves in prose that
integer-coefficient arcs still parametrize the entire purely infinite fiber.
The congruence criterion gives an empty or countably infinite ordinary point
set once a rational parametrization is supplied. These results and the
torsion-free-algebra extension remain **Pending** in Lean; projective
coordinates and later applications were outside that pass. The next pass
reviews Section 17.4, `odg:cr:thm:unimodular` through
`odg:cr:cor:projectiveQ`, and its elliptic example and field-point remark.
The former prose assertion that a principal coordinate ideal implies a rational
point on rational curves was **Needs correction**: `[ω:1]` has unit coordinate
ideal and rational constant-term specialization but is not a `ℚ`-point.
The corrected comparison distinguishes specialization from the point itself
and retains rigidity as the hypothesis of the rational-point conclusion.
The proof now supplies finite inverse-ideal witnesses in a common workspace
and the Gaussian unit factors. These results remain **Pending** in Lean;
That pass leaves Section 17.5 and subsequent geometric applications unreviewed.
The next pass now covers Section 17.5 and Sections 17.6.1–17.6.5, through
`odg:sg:cor:fibre`: the singular-curve criterion, conductor certificate,
boundary place, positive genus, descent and structural consequences.
The former normalization-lifting inference and the assertion that a contracted
differential belongs to the curve function field were **Needs correction**.
The revised proof uses normality in the fraction field as a sufficient lifting
hypothesis and derives commensurability of the contraction's valuation without
claiming field membership. `odg:sg:thm:allcurves` now explicitly requires
`Γ ≠ 0`; otherwise `X = 𝔸¹` is a counterexample. The finite conductor and
polynomial-fiber arguments are expanded. All eleven results in this pass

see the canonical inventory note above. The 86 standard environments below
retain their own ring hypotheses.

### dynamics-and-normal-forms

Source: [surcomplex/dynamics-and-normal-forms/article.tex](surcomplex/dynamics-and-normal-forms/article.tex).

Statements in this newly indexed report remain **pending unless mapped above**.
The finite-word Neumann support lemma and the combinatorial bounds below
are checked; the manuscript correction is recorded separately from that coverage.

**Corrected in the maintained report:** `dyn:cor:ancestry` now retains the
input support `B = supp A`. Its finite pairs `(b,w)` satisfy `b + sum w = γ`,
and its depth bound is `ell_{B,S}(γ)`. The expanded proof counts consecutive
nonempty blocks of each word, establishing strong summability of the operator
iterates and of jointly summable input families under the explicit linear
positive-word hypothesis. The earlier input-independent bound was false:
with `Γ = ℤ`, `S = {1}`, `T(A) = t A`, the input `t^(-n)` contributes
`T^n(t^(-n)) = 1` at output zero, where `ell_S(0) = 0`.
The counterexample and corrected combinatorial bounds are checked in
[Ancestry.lean](../Surreal/HahnSeries/Ancestry.lean); the full operator statement
and downstream analytic results still require separate formal proofs.
The stronger bound in `dyn:prop:linearization` remains valid because its
initial input `L⁻¹f` supplies an initial positive support letter.
The merged report and its README explicitly record this correction; the
original source 03 already retained arbitrary input support in its finite-
dependence claim, and remains accessible in Git history.

The expansion adds 16 pending obligations for resonance flags, fixed-strip
small-divisor solvability and nonlinear normal forms. The external torus
derivatives annihilate Hahn scalars and are distinct from the scalar surreal
derivation. Joint support control and the exact arithmetic hypotheses remain
required beyond the finite-word support lemmas already checked.

Statements in this report remain **pending unless explicitly mapped** in the
implementation table (the sigma-derivation and profile rows). The elementary twisted
product and displacement lemmas can precede the valuation and exponential
results. Later claims retain a total increasing surjective ordered
exponential, a nontrivial convex valuation and any specified stabilization
hypotheses; the existing infinitesimal and finite Hahn exponential does not
supply that global structure. The September 22 source check confirmed the
correspondence with Question 5.4 in the pinned KKS v3 PDF, as recorded in the
report; this is separate from proving the Lean statements. The logarithmic-modulus
classification additionally retains the stated real-closedness hypothesis.

### hahn-evaluation-at-omega

Source: [surreal/hahn-evaluation-at-omega/article.tex](surreal/hahn-evaluation-at-omega/article.tex).

The maintained report corrects `rem:incomparable`: restriction and unique
extension by coefficientwise differences identify unital ring and semiring
maps into a commutative ring. The witnesses give different direct proofs,
not logically incomparable homomorphism obstructions. The new extension
argument remains a separate formalization obligation.

The expanded `thm:exact`, including all four existence alternatives,
strong additivity, the literal evaluation formula and nonzero-input injectivity,
is proved above on the actual universe-indexed carrier. Uniqueness among
coefficient-fixing strongly additive maps and explicit leading data are also
proved. The permitted lower-universe index bound remains visible; no
uniqueness among arbitrary abstract homomorphisms is asserted. The new simple
algebraic extension/root correspondence and intrinsic Laurent-field geometric
convergence likewise remain separate obligations.

statement `prop:topology` now distinguishes full-class set indices from
lower-universe-small indices. The finite cover regression and working
verification runner do not discharge these mathematical proof obligations.

All 56 statements in this report remain **pending**. The three representations
must stay distinct: hereditary computable Conway cuts, effective rational
left-finite series with finite candidate covers, and computable Puiseux series
with one bounded denominator per series. Numerical closure and lifting results
require explicit names, algorithms and moduli; the existing noncomputable Hahn
and normal-form theorems alone do not establish them. Structural classification
and index-complexity claims require computability and descriptive-set-theoretic
inputs. The source's algebraic-root closure corollary retains its explicit
**nonzero polynomial** hypothesis. Its
[reconciliation notes](foundations-and-computation/computable-surreals/MERGE_NOTES.md)
and [review scope](foundations-and-computation/computable-surreals/REVIEW_SCOPE.md)
distinguish imported results, finite checks and the historical repository snapshot

### three-duals-of-hahn-vector-spaces

Source: [surcomplex/three-duals-of-hahn-vector-spaces/article.tex](surcomplex/three-duals-of-hahn-vector-spaces/article.tex).

The main-text proof review covers Sections 1–15. Support and regrouping arguments now
show finite coefficient and triple rearrangements explicitly; the strong-map
classification includes canonical `K`-linearity and the discrete zero-group
case. Completion uses the induced valuation uniformity and an explicit net
of truncations. The cyclic and countable-cofinality boundaries retain their
separate hypotheses; an order unit suffices for `E ⊊ C`, and gives the middle
case only for noncyclic groups. Spherical completeness and contractive
extension now spell out compatibility, ball nesting and the set-sized Zorn
argument. The choice explanation is corrected. Continuous restriction,
separation, quotient kernels, Hilbert norms, Riesz coefficients and the
hyperplane distance arguments are expanded. The review distinguishes positive
from nonnegative operator bounds and a zero orthogonal complement from the
absence of an orthogonal direct-sum complement. Exponent enlargement now
includes the induced-topology dichotomy and unique strong extension;
normal-form interpretation distinguishes scalar outputs from module vectors.
Local source comparisons and targeted primary terminology checks are recorded
in the review ledger. Remaining imports/source reconciliation remain pending.
These are source improvements, not new Lean mappings.

### finite-surreal-probability

Source: [surreal/finite-surreal-probability/article.tex](surreal/finite-surreal-probability/article.tex).

Written in `fb182ea`. The main-text proof review now covers Sections 2–17: scalar
workspaces, residue algebra, finite probability, conditional shadows and
Bayesian updates, logits, softmax, finite information theory, Gibbs laws,
smoothing, logistic separation, finite stochastic processes, infinite addition,
normalized hierarchies, integration, coin obstructions and all-subsets
extensions, the rare latent learning model, standard-part bridges and the
Poisson construction, followed by implementation and scope. Remaining imports
and source reconciliation are pending. The point-weight representation in Section 3 now explicitly assumes
the full event algebra. On a smaller finite algebra only its atom masses are
uniquely determined. Standard-part division requires limited numerator and
denominator with nonzero denominator residue; conditional identities on
zero-mass atoms are interpreted up to versions. The Sections 4–5 review
expands the conditional skeleton and signed coefficient-row proofs, restricts
commuting likelihood updates to a positive joint normalizer, and corrects the
neutral-likelihood wording. The valuation stability clause now stands on its
own positive-event hypothesis; its strict error contract is sufficient, not
necessary for an individual pair of laws. These are source corrections and
clarifications, not new Lean coverage. Sections 6–7 now explicitly require
a positive finite state count and an interior binary prior for logit Bayes.
The logarithmic-score discussion separates its unique interior minimizer
from the unattained boundary infimum over strictly positive predictions.
Softmax stability and concentration, entropy shadows, support inheritance
and equality in data processing have expanded proofs. The Sections 8–9 pass
corrects smoothing to require a positive joint likelihood normalizer for
successive updates and includes the leading coefficient of the chosen scale.
Gibbs minimization, finite path consistency, adapted optional stopping and
Bernoulli variance have expanded proofs, with the zero-horizon cases explicit.
Sections 10–11 now expand common-support and total-variation arguments,
conditional residues and the countable-support positivity boundary. The
expectation bound uses a uniform real bound, rather than only the leading
component's essential bound. Componentwise dominated convergence and product
Fubini are separated from fine convergence and arbitrary Hahn-valued
integration. Posterior coefficients are measurable with a common well-ordered
support, but can fail integrability before density cancellation. Sections 12–13
expand the real coefficient-variation contradictions and keep the logit
argument in the original Hahn coordinates. The relative field embedding,
fine-ultrafilter order and equal-mass symmetry, and finite-fragment atom
splitting are explicit. The all-subsets extension fixes the original field
but does not promise coefficientwise countable additivity. Section 14 now
derives the predictive and posterior updates, gives an elementary fourth-moment
proof of the component strong laws, verifies the full-observation conditional
expectation identity and proves failure of the order-Cauchy criterion on every
path. Typical common-regime paths nevertheless have coefficientwise posterior
limit zero; on the rare tail event the first coefficient diverges. These
ordinary-time limits remain distinct from strong Hahn summation. Two targeted
Section 16 corrections keep the precision contract sufficient and state that
ordered embeddings fixing the reals preserve standard parts. Section 15 now
expands both directions of shadow continuity, the internal-algebra premeasure
argument and uniqueness/completion of its real extension. The Poisson model
specifies finite experiments, internal events and probabilities, and proves
the needed saturation by diagonal selection. An explicit logarithm bound gives
the fixed-count limit, and a measurable ordinary count has exactly the Poisson
law; a Markov bound also excludes mass escaping to infinite counts. Sections
16–17 now distinguish nonnegative weights from regularity and algebraic Brier
scoring from exponential hypotheses. Dependency notes separate imported
product-law existence from the proved Bernoulli strong laws. The scope section
retains finite-support fine-countably-additive laws while declining to assert
a general infinite sampling theory. This completes
the Sections 2–17 main-text pass, not remaining source/provenance reconciliation.
Statements are **pending unless explicitly mapped** in the implementation table.

### omnific-diophantine-geometry

Source: [surreal/omnific-diophantine-geometry/article.tex](surreal/omnific-diophantine-geometry/article.tex).

Sources 01, 02 and 05 were assembled in `bbdd536`. The elementary algebra
comparison, proof review of the original Sections 1–10 and current Sections 14 and 19 and remaining work are recorded in the report
reconciliation. Local sources 06–07 were integrated in `0240140`
(Sections 11–13); subsequent passes review Sections 11–13, including the
witness-closure and coefficient-intersection distinctions, detector and
number-field existential graph, coefficient reconstruction and logical
consequences. Sources 08–09 add Section 15 and clauses
in Sections 17–18 (`b829d8b`). The subsequent denominator review covers
all of Section 15. Further passes cover the Gaussian-fiber and norm
additions in Section 6, source 07's quartic in Section 10 and the
elementary ring/Euler subsections 16.2–16.3, followed by the squarefree
and Weierstrass arguments in Section 16.4. The next pass covers the
two-ring principle, symmetric differentials and inheritance in Section 16.5.
Later reviews cover the curve classification and its applications through
Section 18.6, with the exact source-comparison boundary in the report's
[reconciliation](surreal/omnific-diophantine-geometry/RECONCILIATION.md).
The first C17 pass reviews the elementary lemmas, root-velocity certificate,
translation classification and root corollaries through `odg:disc:rem:comparison`,
plus the polynomial-parameter explanation. Positive degree is explicit in
`odg:disc:cor:omnific` and `odg:disc:cor:roots`; squarefree means over the
coefficient field. A second pass covers `odg:disc:prop:factors` through
`odg:disc:rem:etalenorm`: translation consequences and finite étale units,
including the generic-factor derivations and constant-subalgebra injection.
It retains positive degree in the Galois statement and a nonempty family
in the coherent-translations theorem. The next pass covers monogenic and
arithmetic descent, critical-point and normal-matrix applications, boundary
examples and the splitting-algebra second proof. It handles degree-zero
presentations, makes `n ≥ 1` explicit in the matrix theorem, and distinguishes
simple critical points from distinct critical values. The later question/status
review supplies full faithfulness of base change after `odg:disc:q:etale`, a
sufficient subring inheritance criterion after `odg:disc:q:restricted`, and
the affine-conjugacy criterion `β = h` after `odg:disc:q:dynamics`. These
deductions and the C17-specific theorems remain **Pending** in Lean; shared
support-ring prerequisites are mapped above. Full parallel-source
reconciliation remains pending review.
The ring/retraction proposition
`odg:prop:ring`, degree lemma `odg:lem:degree`, unit/finite-element
proposition `odg:prop:units`, exact floor theorem `odg:thm:floor`,
one-variable rigidity `odg:prop:univariate`, ordinary moduli
`odg:thm:finitequotients`, integer divisors `odg:prop:finitedivisors` and
ordinary primes/mixed gcds/Chinese remainders `odg:cor:mixedgcd`, and
positive-characteristic ideals/finite quotients `odg:cor:charideals`, and
canonical constant extraction `odg:prop:canonicalct` are now **Proved**; other statements below remain **Pending** unless mapped.
The separately styled cited theorem
`odg:fact:settarget` is also in scope, outside the standard-environment table.

### set-sized-quotients-of-omnific-integers

Source: [surreal/set-sized-quotients-of-omnific-integers/article.tex](surreal/set-sized-quotients-of-omnific-integers/article.tex).

The twenty-four-manuscript assembly has 409 standard statements and
nine separately styled principal summaries. The four batch-34 companions contribute 105
standard statements on class residue fields, semialgebraic preservers,
polyhedral-cone cores and henselian branching, all **Pending** in Lean and
independent proof review. The two expanded principal summaries do not
extend proof coverage of their earlier clauses.


Merged report written in `7494d53` (batch 24: eight manuscripts, base 06) and
extended by batch 25 (local sources 12–16) and batch 26 (17–19,
`aae58bb`); this index covers the written
`article.tex`. An initial proof review covers the elementary ring and support
lemmas, collision/telescope/division arguments and the universal quotient
theorem, plus `osq:cor:nofield`. The next pass covers the sixteen standard
results from `osq:cor:Oz` through `osq:cor:dense`: representations, residual
targets, small quotients, principal ideals and finite-congruence closure.
Later classifications and full parallel-source reconciliation remain pending. See the [review record](surreal/set-sized-quotients-of-omnific-integers/RECONCILIATION.md).
The original unrestricted integer clause of `osq:prop:common`(iv) was
**Needs correction**: in characteristic p, pΠ = 0 while Π is nonzero. The
maintained statement now requires the integer to have nonzero image in the
coefficient field. The general nonzero-coefficient assertion is unchanged.
The proof of `osq:lem:separation`(iii) now uses the set-sized endomorphism
ring for noncommutative sources; the direct bound by module size retains
commutativity. Shared elementary Lean prerequisites are mapped under the
sibling report's labels above; the class quotient and cardinal results here
remain **Pending** in Lean.

The original assertion in `osq:prop:principal` that a nonconstant principal
quotient itself admits no set-sized quotient is **Needs correction**:
`Oz/(ω)` surjects onto `ℤ`. The maintained statement says instead that
`A/(f)` cannot itself be realized as a set-sized ring. Its universal set-sized
image is `D/(ct(f))`; this corrected class-size assertion remains **Pending**
in Lean. The new unnumbered nonunital Gaussian representation consequence
classifies maps by pairs `(e,j)` satisfying `e²=e`, `ej=je=j`, `j²=−e`; it
also remains **Pending** in Lean. These manuscript additions create no new
implementation mapping.

The next review covers the seven standard results from `osq:cor:primeexample`
through `osq:prop:conservative`, together with their adjacent examples. The
primality input was checked against L’Innocente–Mantova v5, Theorem B; it
remains imported. Completion proofs now give the compatible residue maps,
Gaussian rank-two coordinates, kernels, diagonal images and density. The real
omnific completion and topology mappings under `odg:eq:profinite` above retain
their proved scope; this review adds no Gaussian completion mapping.
The localization and presentation properties now explicitly use unital `Hom₁`.
Under a nonunital reading of `Hom`, the original empty-Hom assertion in
`osq:thm:localization` is **Needs correction**: the zero map from the zero
ring to any nonzero ring is a counterexample. The maintained statement removes
that ambiguity. The added general positive existential retraction consequence,
including Gaussian coefficients, has no new implementation mapping here.
The following pass reviews the nine standard results from `osq:thm:modules`
through `osq:lem:midempotent`: exactness and projectivity with explicit size
conventions, derivations into small modules, coefficient-weighted class
derivations, and the finite-side residue theorem and its consequences.
The finite-side corollary now explicitly restricts to set-sized unital modules
and unital ring targets. Its universal proof is a Hartogs collision and also
handles nonunital additive multiplicative maps, as an unnumbered consequence.
The Gaussian 2-torsion calculation retains the nonzero F₂ example. The
Berarducci–Mantova normalization was checked against v3, page 2; its existence
remains imported. These manuscript reviews and the new explanation of nonzero
Q-derivations of R add no Lean implementation mappings. Existing Hahn Euler
and actual standard-part prerequisites retain their stated scope. The class
universal properties remain **Pending** in Lean. Later support/cardinal
results and full parallel-source reconciliation remain pending review.

The next pass reviews `osq:thm:support`, `osq:prop:monomialbounds`,
`osq:prop:fieldbound`, `osq:thm:criterion`, `osq:thm:coinitial` and
`osq:lem:cyclic`, including the adjacent threshold examples. The original
unqualified replacement by `B^{<λ}` in the finite-side extension criterion
`osq:thm:support`(iv) is **Needs correction** if λ=ℵ₀ is allowed: augmentation
extends to that same finite-support ring and still fails to factor through
standard part. The corrected term is `B^{<μ⁺}` for infinite μ, matching the
positive-side at-most-μ support bound. Part (ii) now specifies that the
monomial belongs to the stated domain. `osq:main:support` names ct and st
on their respective sides; the module clause of the monomial bound specifies
h>0. Support estimates handle singular uncountable bounds without regularity.
The field bound requires an appropriate positive monomial divisor for its
general-element conclusion. The two example thresholds include both lower
bounds and attaining representations. These results remain **Pending** in
Lean; no implementation mappings are added. The later organizing theorem,
its model classifications and full source reconciliation remain pending review.

The countable-support two-armed construction is reviewed next: the six
standard results `osq:lem:hcfield`, `osq:lem:twosided`,
`osq:lem:smallcommon`, `osq:lem:card03`, `osq:thm:model03` and
`osq:lem:cardinalfacts`, including the adjacent integer-part and continuum
examples. The original Gaussian alternative in `osq:thm:model03`(i) is
**Needs correction** as written: its fraction field contains i, whereas the
printed real field `F^{03}_κ` does not. The maintained statement explicitly
pairs each ring with its real or complex field. Its direct proof gives the
exact ring/module detection threshold, ideal generator count, flatness,
idempotence, nonflat constant quotient and stated Tor vanishing, without
depending on the later five-model summary. Hahn closedness and directed
colimits of flat modules remain imported facts, checked against the cited
L’Innocente–Mantova Fact 2.1.1 and Stacks Lemma 10.39.3. All six results
remain **Pending** in Lean; no implementation mappings are added. The
other four models, the organizing theorem across all five models, later
classifications and full source reconciliation remain pending review.

The next review covers source 06's five standard results
`osq:lem:kappagap`, `osq:prop:fieldclosure`, `osq:prop:kappachain`,
`osq:lem:card06` and `osq:thm:model06`, plus `osq:ex:CH`. The original
discreteness proof's assertion that any nonzero series with positive
leading exponent exceeds every real is **Needs correction**: `-X^g`
for g>0 is negative. The corrected proof requires a positive leading
coefficient; the proposition's statement is unchanged. Field closure uses
one small rational span and remains valid at singular uncountable support
bounds. An explicit series on a cofinal sequence of shrinking exponents
shows why the positive-monomial-divisor property can fail at singular κ.
The subset cardinality is proved by coding graphs, and the exact detection
threshold is derived directly, with identity/regular-module attainment and
an explicit Gaussian argument. The ℵ₁ example gives the actual exponent
reindexing isomorphism between the two models. These results and the new
unnumbered singular-bound counterexample remain **Pending** in Lean.
Poonen's Corollary 4 remains the imported closedness input; the corresponding
small-span proof in the first-kappa report was compared for notation and
hypotheses. No implementation mappings are added. The remaining three
models, the five-model summary, later classifications and full parallel-source
reconciliation remain pending review.

The next pass reviews the four standard controlled-field results
`osq:lem:gammabounds`, `osq:lem:controlled`, `osq:lem:finitecoord` and
`osq:thm:model08`, with their embedding and residue-field consequences.
The relative real closure and the count of initial-segment truncations are
explicit. Finite coordinate use is tracked through rational operations,
algebraic roots and truncations; the countably supported series with one
term in each of the coordinates e_n is excluded. The actual subring is
written as the image under Φ before the Hahn/surreal identification is used.
The proof's unqualified formula nΠ = Π is **Needs correction** at n=0;
the maintained argument explicitly uses only nonzero integers and division
by their constants. No theorem statement changes. Quotient alternatives
include the zero ring and may overlap when κ=ℵ₀. Exact generator counts,
ring/module threshold attainment, positive-characteristic residue fields,
and existence and size of characteristic-zero residue fields are proved
directly, with ω mapping to -1 in the specified quotient. All four results
and the added unnumbered consequences remain **Pending** in Lean. The
other two models, the full five-model summary, later classifications and
parallel-source reconciliation remain pending review.

The source-09 pass reviews the four standard results `osq:lem:tail`,
`osq:thm:barrier`, `osq:lem:coefffield` and `osq:thm:residue`, with
construction, exact generator count and `osq:rem:fstar`. The maintained
claim that λ^ℵ₀=λ alone implies λ≥2^ℵ₀ is **Needs correction**: λ=0 and
λ=1 are counterexamples. Infinitude is now explicit in the construction,
the organizing table, the principal summary `osq:main:thresholds`, and the
comparison in `osq:rem:reconcile`; the source's stronger continuum lower
bound was already sufficient. Only the principal summary changes among
numbered theorem/lemma/proposition/corollary statements. The tail uses
regularity of ω₁ rather than λ. Cardinal counting, ordered embeddings,
nonunital ring and module separation, coefficient-field recovery,
pairwise comaximal ideals, exact field/module thresholds, finite residual,
zero Jacobson radical and the ℵ₁ generator count have expanded proofs.
The unrestricted-support counterexample now explicitly checks the
negative exponent in each putative monomial quotient. All four standard
results and these consequences remain **Pending** in Lean. The source-11
model, full organizing theorem, later classifications and full parallel-
source reconciliation remain pending review; no implementation mapping
is added by this manuscript pass.

The source-11 and organizing pass reviews the three standard statements
`osq:prop:lex`, `osq:prop:card11` and `osq:thm:thresholds`, with the
comparison `osq:rem:reconcile`. Field closure uses the subgroup generated
by finitely many small supports and needs only uncountability; regularity
supplies the gaps and the union-of-supports generator obstruction. The
lower bound encodes subsets by coefficient-one series even in positive
characteristic, and the upper bound separately counts finite and infinite
supports. Explicit injections and witnesses give equality of the sizes of
the smaller-scale field, ideal, ring and ambient field, and exact ring and
module detection. The principal-ideal chain is strictly increasing and
proves idempotence and exactly κ generators. The organizing theorem checks
all five smaller-scale fields before applying the gap argument, with
nonunital maps, module orbits, unique constant-term factorization and both
quotient cases included.

The introduction's blanket claim that every coefficient choice is an
omnific subring is **Needs correction**: source 11 allows D=K=F_p,
so a unital embedding into a characteristic-zero omnific ring is
impossible. The maintained introduction restricts that claim to the
displayed real/integer and Gaussian instances. No numbered theorem
statement changes. The comparison now distinguishes realized size θ
from support parameter κ and proves (κ^{<κ})^ℵ₀=κ^{<κ} for regular
uncountable κ; this supports the claim that only source 08 reaches
non-fixed sizes, even with source 11's smaller coefficient fields.
All three reviewed results and the unnumbered consequences remain
**Pending** in Lean. The homological package, including the Ext clause
of the principal summary, later classifications and full parallel-source
reconciliation remain pending review. No implementation mapping is added.

The homological pass reviews `osq:lem:projideal`, all seven clauses of
`osq:thm:homological`, and `osq:thm:extthreshold`, including the Ext clause
of `osq:main:thresholds`. The decomposition in (H1) is explicitly additive,
and nonsplitting in clause (vi) explicitly means nonsplitting of A-modules;
the ring and additive sections already exist. This is the only changed
numbered statement, a category clarification rather than a changed
mathematical conclusion. The projective-ideal proof constructs its finite
generating family from a split free module. The package spells out the
filtered union, tensor balancing, the nonflatness resolution, projective
base change, and the cochain adjunction. A comparison map verifies that
the resulting natural Ext isomorphisms are inverse to inflation, without
assuming flatness of D over A. Schanuel's lemma, the nonsplit first
extension, and the dimension-shift splice give explicit nonvanishing.

A fully described countable telescope verifies pd_A D=2 in that case;
the general exact projective dimension remains undetermined. Cardinal
counting uses finite support in the free presentation to produce a
degree-two coefficient module of size exactly |A|. The same size holds
for A/xA in all five models when x is nonzero in I: otherwise I=xA would
contradict nonfinite generation. The flat-colimit and projective-module
inputs were checked against the Stacks Project (Tags 05UT, 05CF, 00O3;
Section 15.60 for flat resolutions). All three reviewed results and the
unnumbered consequences remain **Pending** in Lean. Later core/tensor
classifications and full parallel-source reconciliation remain pending
review. No implementation mapping is added by this manuscript pass.

The finite-support core pass reviews eight results:
`osq:hd:lem:cores`, `osq:hd:prop:finite`, `osq:hd:lem:faces`,
`osq:hd:thm:resolution`, `osq:hd:cor:arithmeticTor`,
`osq:hd:prop:etale`, `osq:hd:thm:boolean` and `osq:hd:cor:fd`.
No numbered statements change. The proofs exhibit the finite polynomial
subalgebras and coefficient-preserving embeddings, unique finite-target
factorization, compatible quotient systems and the p-adic kernel.
Strict exponent subtraction keeps arbitrary K coefficients in the tail
when exhausting a face ideal by principal ideals. The explicit simplex
contraction proves degreewise exactness without asserting an A-linear
splitting; finite support justifies its use also in countable rank.

The Boolean Tor computation is performed on the quotient complex after
tensoring, with all four exponent cases and their contractions written
out. At a singleton unit exponent the map is K → K/D, with kernel D;
higher surviving faces have coefficient module K. Dimension shifting
gives both exact flat dimensions, including infinite rank. Nilpotent
lifting uses idempotence; nonflatness and failure of finite presentation
have separate proofs. The reduced differential module is explicitly
distinguished from differentials for the map in the opposite direction.
These eight results remain **Pending** in Lean. The existing exact
finite-grid audit is supporting evidence only for its stated rational
coefficient test pair, not a proof of the general formula. Later lattice,
tensor and derived classifications and full source reconciliation remain
pending review; this pass adds no implementation mapping.
